chapter: 1977: Kansas City honor and the piano
title: Bobby Henderson as one of his favorite pianists
summary: Basie clarifies that Bobby Henderson, whom he first heard with Billie Holiday, was one of his favorites, along with James P. Johnson, the Lion and Fats.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: I read you said that -- I read your-- that Bobby Henderson was your favorite piano player.
Bobby was great. I didn't say he was my favorite, he was one of my favorites. I could never point out no one particular of my favorite for everything, because he was one of my favorite piano players.
The first I got a taste of him was with Lady Day.
: Where did you hear her?
I don't know where it was, somewhere.
I think it was in Albany.
: You don't mean some place like (inaudible). No, it couldn't have been, could it?
No.
: Yeah, it could have been. But it wasn't, because you first heard her in '36 at Monroe's.
Right.
: Okay. What hit you about his playing?
What hit me?
Yeah, what hit you?
The way he played period.
You saw him up in Albany?
I just can't remember. You are talking about damn near 35 years ago. The hell you ain't.
I'm not, the sixties, the fifties or sixties.
What, 25 years?
Well, that's recent history, isn't it?
No. I can't remember actually.
Then maybe she was up in Albany or Ithaca or something. Because if you say you heard him play for her, then you heard him play for her.
Well, anyway, I did read a quotation in many places, that he was "my favorite piano player." But he was one.
Yeah.
To clear the record.

Yeah, of course, during those times there were a whole lot of guys that were playing that were favorite guys I liked to listen to. That's Guys during the time of James P. Johnson, the Lion and Fats and all those guys. And hadn't yet gotten to Earl Hines.
You hadn't?
No, because I hadn't -- you know, I (inaudible) [hadn't been exposed to him enough.]
At that point?
